purpose: Machine-readable realization matrix from constrained-activity meta model to Visual SceneMaker SceneFlow concepts.

metaToSceneFlow.description: Condition that controls when the constrained activity stops.
realizationRules: Use IEDGE for interrupt/event style constraints.
Use CEDGE for state/value guard constraints.
Constraint exit edge should originate at supernode for immediate reactive exit.
invariants: Constraint variable exists or is auto-created according to mode.

metaToSceneFlow.description: Behavior executed while constraint is unsatisfied.

kinds.sceneFlowPattern: Waiting cycle with one or more activity nodes (music/picture/etc.) connected via TEDGE/FEDGE.
Waiting cycle with socially assistive action nodes and policy gates.

invariants: At least one active internal loop exists while waiting.
All activity nodes belong to the constrained-activity supernode.

metaToSceneFlow.description: Controls timing, repetition, escalation, and interruption behavior.

policyMapping.sceneFlowRealization: counter variable + update command + CEDGE guard
levelled subflow/supernode stages with transition guards

metaToSceneFlow.description: Transition behavior once constraint is satisfied.
realizationRules: Create/reuse continuation node at parent level.
Set exit edge target to continuation node id (never node name).
invariants: Exit edge has valid target node id.
No child-node edge targets outside supernode scope.

ruleDefinitions.description: IR operation list must not be empty.
Each operation entry must be a valid object.
Each operation must define its kind.
Operation type must be supported by the IR compiler.
Node creation requires a node id.
Node ids must be unique in snapshot+patch scope.
Node references in operations must be provided.
Node references must resolve to known nodes.
Edge creation requires an edge id.
Edge ids must be unique in snapshot+patch scope.
Edge references in updates/deletes must be provided.
Edge references must resolve to known edges.
Edge type must be one of the supported SceneFlow edge types.
Edge type must be allowed by capability snapshot.
Conditional/interrupt edges must provide conditionText.
Timed edges must provide timeoutMs.
Timed edge timeout must be non-negative.
Probabilistic edges must provide probability.
Probability must be in range [0,100].
Node-in-supernode edges must not target outside that supernode scope.
Variable definition operation requires varDef payload.
Variable definition requires name.
Variable definition type must be supported.
Condition expressions may only reference known variables.

A PlayScene command with a literal scene name should refer to a scene the project declares. Only literal names are checked: a name given as a variable or computed at runtime, such as PlayScene("Topic_" + topic), is not knowable statically and is left alone. Warning rather than error because a scene may legitimately be authored after the flow that plays it.

Command text must use double quotes for strings. A bare single quote is rejected by the lexer and the contents are then read as an identifier, so PlayScene('greet') compiles silently into a reference to a variable named greet. Error rather than warning because there is no case in which a bare single quote is correct. Single quotes inside a double-quoted string, as in embedded action text, are allowed.
Supernode exit edges must target nodes outside the originating supernode scope.
Constrained wait supernodes must keep at least one internal active timed loop alive.
Violation code emitted when supernode exit target remains inside supernode scope.
Violation code emitted when constrained supernode has no internal liveness flow.

globalInvariants: All created node positions are visible and non-overlapping where possible.
Generated flow compiles and passes semantic validation.
